newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shares in Nigerian trading end week bullishly.
newsitem.headline: Shares in Nigerian trading end week bullishly.

text.p: Equities ended the week in bullish fashion at the Nigerian stock market on Friday and traders said similar trend would continue next week.
Due to technical problems the all-share index was not updated.
Traders said shares soared as investors continued to be attracted to the market making some 47 equities appreciate at Friday's trading.
"Most buyers were active in the banking, food and beverages, conglomerates and petroleum sectors although there was growing enthusiasm for industrial goods and insurance companies," one trader said.
"Rising prices will remain a regular feature for sometime unless a sudden negative development occurs. There is plenty of money in the system to throw on shares," he added.
Shares of conglomerates PZ with an improved half-year result on Thursday surged to 23.80 naira, up by 30 kobo. Lever Brothers was also 30 kobo up at 21.80 naira.
Nestle at 63.30 naira and Nigerian Bottling Company at 46.10 naira were each 50 kobo better while Cadbury climbed 40 kobo to 34.40 naira.
Agip was the biggest beneficiary among the oil marketers with a 50 kobo gain at 29.60 naira while National Oil went 45 kobo higher at 59.05 naira.
Ashaka Cement shed 30 kobo to 13.50 naira due to continual difficulties it is encountering in selling its products, according to traders.
Dwindling fortunes cost Chemical and Allied Products three kobo to 4.40 naira while Thomas Wyatt lost 10 kobo at 5.00 naira on large dumping of its shares.
Analysts said bank shares, alongside the regular gainers, were set to rise further next week with the market continuing to enjoy an upswing.

"It is difficult to see the market slump in the immediate future because investors are on a buying spree," one said, adding: "Only isolated off-loading of individual companies will be evident and this will be based strictly on the interplay of market forces."
